body.working_title: TBATS in smooth: formulation, rationale and performance on the M4 hourly data

body.text: Is the TBATS of smooth, which places each trigonometric harmonic in the linear ARIMA slot of ADAM's state-space core as two states with lags 1 and 2, the same model as De Livera, Hyndman and Snyder's TBATS, and where does it differ from it by design?

How accurate are the point forecasts and the prediction intervals of smooth's TBATS on the M4 hourly series, against forecast::tbats, statsforecast's AutoTBATS, ADAM ETS and seasonal naive, and how long does it take?

body.definition: TBATS of the smooth package (R tbats(), Python TBATS), a linear single-source-of-error model in the Box-Cox space: y_t^(lambda) = w' v_{t-l} + e_t, v_t = F v_{t-l} + g e_t, with an ETS(A,N,N), ETS(A,A,N) or ETS(A,Ad,N) level and trend, and for each period m_i and harmonic j = 1..k_i (lambda_ij = 2 pi j / m_i) two states with lags 1 and 2 in the ARIMA slot of ADAM's core: u_t = v_{1,t-1} + v_{2,t-2}, v_{k,t} = eta_k u_t + g_k e_t with eta = (2 cos lambda_ij, -1) and g = (gamma_1i, sin(lambda_ij) gamma_2i - cos(lambda_ij) gamma_1i), so that (1 - 2 cos lambda_ij B + B^2) u_t = (g_1 B + g_2 B^2) e_t; an optional ADAM ARMA component (an additive state block, not ARMA errors); lambda in [0, 1] estimated by likelihood with the Jacobian; harmonics preselected by information criterion on a global OLS model of the Box-Cox series on Fourier terms; trend and ARMA orders selected by AICc.

TBATS of De Livera, Hyndman and Snyder (2011, JASA): y_t^(lambda) = l_{t-1} + phi b_{t-1} + sum_i sum_j s^(i)_{j,t-1} + d_t, l_t = l_{t-1} + phi b_{t-1} + alpha d_t, b_t = phi b_{t-1} + beta d_t, s^(i)_{j,t} = cos(lambda_ij) s^(i)_{j,t-1} + sin(lambda_ij) s*^(i)_{j,t-1} + gamma_1i d_t, s*^(i)_{j,t} = -sin(lambda_ij) s^(i)_{j,t-1} + cos(lambda_ij) s*^(i)_{j,t-1} + gamma_2i d_t, with ARMA(p, q) errors d_t = sum phi_k d_{t-k} + sum theta_k e_{t-k} + e_t.

The tbats() function of the R package forecast (Hyndman et al.), De Livera et al.'s TBATS with its own model selection, called with seasonal.periods = c(24, 168), single-threaded, otherwise default settings.
AutoTBATS of the Python package statsforecast (Nixtla), called with season_length = [24, 168], otherwise default settings.
ADAM ETS of smooth's Python port, ADAM(model='ZXZ', lags=[24, 168]) with its default settings: ETS with a daily and a weekly seasonal component selected by AICc.
Seasonal naive forecast repeating the last 168 observations (the last week) of the training sample.

The 414 hourly series of the M4 competition (Makridakis et al., 2020), training samples of 700 or 960 observations and test samples of 48, from the Mcompetitions/M4-methods repository (Dataset/Train/Hourly-train.csv, Dataset/Test/Hourly-test.csv).
The M4 hourly training samples with their last 48 observations held out as a validation test: fitting on observations 1..n-48 and evaluating on n-47..n; never the official test samples.
Each method is fitted once to each training sample and forecasts h = 1..48 steps ahead from its end; no refits, no rolling origin.
Mean absolute scaled error of a series: mean over h = 1..48 of |y_{n+h} - f_{n+h}| divided by the in-sample mean absolute seasonal difference at lag 24, as in M4.
Geometric mean over series of MASE(method A)/MASE(method B); below 1 means A is more accurate. Its 95% confidence interval is exp of the t-interval of the mean log ratio over series.
Share of the 414 x 48 test values inside the 95% prediction interval of a method.
Wall-clock seconds to fit a method to one training sample and produce its forecasts and intervals, single-threaded.

body.text: The independent De Livera implementation reads smooth's initial Fourier coefficients one step later: smooth's coefficients (a, b) define s(t) = a sin(lambda t) + b cos(lambda t) with s(1) entering y_1, whereas De Livera's state s_0 enters y_1, so s_0 = a sin(lambda) + b cos(lambda) and s*_0 = a cos(lambda) - b sin(lambda). RN1 compared the recursions with s_0 = b (a time-origin mismatch of the initial states, not of the recursion); RN2 uses the conversion. The recursion equations of the independent implementation were not changed.
With the conversion, the fitted values agree to 1.7e-14 on the 72 exploratory cases of seeds 1 and 2; H2 and H3 checks behave as stated.
forecast::tbats is run from forecast 9.0.1 (the last release for R 4.3.3, the R that this container's apt provides; forecast 9.0.2 needs a newer R), with statsforecast 2.1.1 for AutoTBATS.

body.definition: Deterministic checks of smooth TBATS against its specification, per seed: (H1) random parameters, initial states and series of 300 observations simulated by De Livera's recursion with normal errors, for the periods {24}, {7.3}, {24, 168}, {7.3, 30.4}, no/additive/damped trend and lambda in {1, 0.5, 0}, fitted by smooth TBATS with all parameters and initial states fixed; (H2) a noise-free series of 300 observations made of a random level and random harmonics of the periods 7.3 and 24, fitted with random fixed persistence and initial='backcasting'; (H3) nine random pairs of alpha in (0.05, 0.95) and |phi| in (0.05, 0.95) for a local level with AR(1), the impulse response w'F^(j-1)g at j = 1..20 read from the fitted model's matrices. Code: claimset-code/smooth-tbats/formulation_checks.py.

body.design: One run of claimset-code/smooth-tbats/formulation_checks.py --seeds 101 102 103 104 105 106 107 108 109 110 --n 300 (TM14) on the code branch's committed code: H1 on 10 x 36 = 360 random cases; H2 on 10 random noise-free series; H3 on 90 random (alpha, phi) pairs. Python port of smooth from this repository, numpy and NLopt as installed (DC3).
body.analysis: The script writes, over all cases of the run: the max relative difference of the fitted values of smooth TBATS from the De Livera recursion (relative to max(|fitted|, 1)); the max absolute in-sample error over the noise-free series; the max absolute difference of smooth's impulse response from alpha + phi^j; and, over cases, the min of the max absolute difference from the ARMA-errors response phi^j + alpha (1 - phi^j)/(1 - phi).
body.new_data: Seeds 101-110 were not used before (RN1, RN2 and RN4 used seeds 1, 2 and 3): they draw new parameters, initial states and series for H1, new noise-free series (level, harmonics and coefficients) and persistence for H2, and new (alpha, phi) pairs for H3, replacing the fixed series and the fixed 3 x 3 grid of RN1.

parameters.sample: 10 seeds (101-110), one run, no stopping rule; the checks are deterministic given the seeds

h1.variable: max relative difference of fitted values over all cases, smooth TBATS vs De Livera recursion

h2.variable: max absolute in-sample error over all noise-free series, backcasting

h3_adam.variable: max absolute difference of smooth's impulse response from alpha + phi^j over all cases

h3_errors.variable: min over cases of the max absolute difference of smooth's impulse response from the ARMA-errors response

body.design: One run of claimset-code/smooth-tbats/m4_hourly.py --train SR1 --test SR2 --split test --workers 4 on the code branch's committed code, with the software of DC3: each of smooth TBATS (TBATS(lags=[1, 24, 168]) with its defaults, h = 48, 95% prediction intervals), forecast::tbats (TM3), AutoTBATS (TM4), ADAM ETS (TM5) and seasonal naive 168 (TM6) is fitted once to each of the 414 M4 hourly training samples and forecasts the 48 test values (TM9), each fit single-threaded, the series spread over 4 worker processes (forecast::tbats in R first, then the Python methods). A method that fails on a series (an error or non-finite forecasts) gets the seasonal naive 168 forecasts for it and no interval, its test values counting as uncovered; the failures are reported per method.
body.analysis: Per series and method: MASE (TM10), the coverage of the 95% interval (TM12), the elapsed time (TM13). Relative MASE (TM11) of smooth TBATS to each comparator with its 95% t-interval on the log scale, the relative elapsed time to forecast::tbats likewise; four one-sided t-tests on the mean log ratios (H4: vs forecast::tbats, H0 log ratio >= log 1.05; H5: vs AutoTBATS, same; H6: vs seasonal naive 168, H0 >= 0; H7: time vs forecast::tbats, H0 >= 0), their p-values adjusted by Holm over the four. The coverage of smooth TBATS over all 414 x 48 test values. Also reported, not deciding: mean and median MASE, mean sMAPE, median time and failures per method, and the relative MASE to ADAM ETS.

exclusions.name: zero_mase
exclusions.rule: a series whose MASE is zero or non-finite for smooth TBATS or for the comparator (its log ratio is not finite) is left out of that comparison's relative MASE and test; reported per comparator as 'series excluded by zero MASE'

parameters.test: one-sided one-sample t-test on the per-series log ratios (smooth TBATS over the comparator) of MASE (H4-H6) or elapsed time (H7), H0: mean log ratio >= log(1.05) against forecast::tbats and AutoTBATS (H4, H5), >= 0 against seasonal naive 168 (H6) and for the time (H7)
parameters.sample: All 414 series of the official M4 hourly test split, fixed by the data set; one run, no interim analysis. For orientation: with a standard deviation of the per-series log ratio of 0.3, the standard error of the mean log ratio is 0.015, so a true relative MASE of 1 lies 3.3 standard errors below the non-inferiority margin log(1.05).

p_ftbats.variable: Holm-adjusted p-value, one-sided t-test, smooth TBATS vs forecast::tbats (MASE)

p_autotbats.variable: Holm-adjusted p-value, one-sided t-test, smooth TBATS vs AutoTBATS (MASE)

p_snaive.variable: Holm-adjusted p-value, one-sided t-test, smooth TBATS vs seasonal naive 168 (MASE)

p_time.variable: Holm-adjusted p-value, one-sided t-test, smooth TBATS vs forecast::tbats (time)

body.design: One run of claimset-code/smooth-tbats/m4_hourly.py --train SR1 --test SR2 --split test --workers 4 on the code branch's committed code (commit 3444dda or later with the same script), with the software of DC3: each of smooth TBATS (TBATS(lags=[1, 24, 168]) with its defaults, h = 48, 95% prediction intervals), forecast::tbats (TM3), AutoTBATS (TM4), ADAM ETS (TM5) and seasonal naive 168 (TM6) is fitted once to each of the 414 M4 hourly training samples and forecasts the 48 test values (TM9), each fit single-threaded, the series spread over 4 worker processes (forecast::tbats in R first, then the Python methods). A method that fails on a series (an error or non-finite forecasts) gets the seasonal naive 168 forecasts for it and no interval, its test values counting as uncovered; the failures are reported per method.
body.analysis: Per series and method: MASE (TM10), the coverage of the 95% prediction interval (TM12), the elapsed time (TM13). Relative MASE (TM11) of smooth TBATS to each comparator with its 99% t-interval on the log scale, the relative elapsed time to forecast::tbats likewise; four one-sided t-tests on the mean log ratios at alpha = 0.01 (H4: vs forecast::tbats, H0 log ratio >= log 1.05; H5: vs AutoTBATS, same; H6: vs seasonal naive 168, H0 >= 0; H7: time vs forecast::tbats, H0 >= 0), their p-values adjusted by Holm over the four. The coverage of smooth TBATS over all 414 x 48 test values (H8). The Nemenyi test (TM15, rmcb, level 0.99) on the per-series MASE of the five methods: mean ranks and critical distance (H9). Also reported, not deciding: mean and median MASE, mean sMAPE, median time and failures per method, the relative MASE to ADAM ETS, and rmcb's p-value of equal mean ranks.
body.new_data: H9 is tested on the official M4 hourly test samples (SR2), which no run has read: the exploratory runs RN3, RN5 and RN7 fitted and evaluated the validation split of the training samples only (m4_hourly.py reads the test file only with --split test).

exclusions.name: zero_mase
exclusions.rule: a series whose MASE is zero or non-finite for smooth TBATS or for the comparator (its log ratio is not finite) is left out of that comparison's relative MASE and t-test; reported per comparator as 'series excluded by zero MASE'. The Nemenyi test ranks all 414 series.

parameters.test: one-sided one-sample t-test on the per-series log ratios (smooth TBATS over the comparator) of MASE (H4-H6) or elapsed time (H7), H0: mean log ratio >= log(1.05) against forecast::tbats and AutoTBATS (H4, H5), >= 0 against seasonal naive 168 (H6) and for the time (H7); their intervals are 99% t-intervals. H9: the Nemenyi test (greybox rmcb, distribution='tukey', level 0.99, ranks averaged over ties) on the per-series MASE of the five methods, with its own family-wise control over the pairwise comparisons (not in the Holm family)
parameters.correction: holm over the four t-tests of H4-H7; the Nemenyi test's own control for H9
parameters.sample: All 414 series of the official M4 hourly test split, fixed by the data set; one run, no interim analysis. For orientation: with a standard deviation of the per-series log ratio of 0.3, the standard error of the mean log ratio is 0.015, so a true relative MASE of 1 lies 3.3 standard errors below the non-inferiority margin log(1.05).

body.text: Ivan Svetunkov (AC2) judged sMAPE and MASE unsuitable for this study and set RMSSE as its only accuracy measure, scaled by the in-sample root mean squared first difference (lag 1), after the confirmatory run RN8 had been seen. sMAPE was the agent's own choice, never requested, and is dropped from the code (commit d359020); MASE is replaced by RMSSE in m4_hourly.py (commit after d359020). The hypotheses stated on MASE (H4, H5, H6, H9) are restated on RMSSE and tested under a new plan on the same test split; the sMAPE and MASE results already recorded stay in this append-only record and are not reported as findings.
